title: At the edge of the abyss
caption: The dwarf spiral galaxy NGC 6503, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6503 · constellation Draco · about 17 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Pink puffs dot the swirling arms of NGC 6503 in this Hubble image, marking places where new stars have recently formed. The galaxy is like a smaller version of the Milky Way, and it sits near a vast, nearly empty region of space.

Although its structure resembles our galaxy's, NGC 6503's disc spans just 30 000 light-years, about a third of the Milky Way's size, so astronomers classify it as a dwarf spiral. It lies roughly 17 million light-years away in the constellation Draco, and Arthur Auwers discovered it in July 1854.

The galaxy is perched at the edge of the Local Void, a giant hollow in space bordered by the Hercules and Coma galaxy clusters and by our own Local Group. Estimates of the void's size vary widely, from 30 million light-years across to over 150 million, so NGC 6503 has very little galactic company nearby.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.27 x 1.84 arcminutes) and distance (17 million light years), the frame spans roughly 16,000 × 9,100 light-years. Its light set out about 17 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Red shows light from glowing hydrogen gas in star-forming regions, and blue shows near-infrared light, colored that way for contrast.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and the pink and blue coloring here comes from the chosen filters rather than the galaxy's natural appearance.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble and NASA

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Its isolation led stargazer Stephen James O'Meara to give it a nickname, the Lost-In-Space Galaxy, in his book Hidden Treasures.
The unusual color balance comes from unusual filters, with 28 minutes through a filter that passes only hydrogen emission and 12 minutes in near-infrared light.
alt: A spiral galaxy with swirling arms dotted with pink puffs of star formation.
